rationale: The claim accurately reflects the content and language of the MAA/RN/2025/04 notice. The notice explicitly states that "For Certified Air Systems, the Applicant should raise a Military Certification Review Item (MCRI) for MAA agreement" (p. 2, para 6) and "It is recommended that early applications of ML techniques... use... models that then remain fixed for system integration and use within a defined operational design domain" (p. 2, para 7). The claim's use of "should" and "recommends" directly matches the source. The notice itself is described as "informative correspondence" and "guidance" (p. 1, para 2), aligning with the claim's description of an "assurance path" and recommendations. The claim's scope correctly limits it to UK military aviation guidance and explicitly excludes civil-airworthiness approval, addressing a key part of the challenge.
evidence_locators: S-CHAL-001-R1: PDF pp. 1–2, paragraphs 2–4, Scope, Implementation and Background
S-CHAL-001-R2: PDF pp. 2–3, paragraphs 6–7, Certified Air Systems
limitations: The challenge to obtain and inspect the MAA's underlying MMAC/MCRI material and a completed public MCRI could not be fulfilled with the supplied review packet, as this material is noted as applicant-specific and non-public. This prevents a definitive determination of whether "should raise an MCRI" translates to a strict, universally mandatory requirement in all contexts for certified systems, beyond the guidance provided in the notice.

The review is limited to the provided MAA/RN/2025/04 document and does not include other MAA Regulatory Publications (MRP) or the Manual of Military Air System Certification (MMAC) referenced in the notice.
